title: Keep a message the link can't carry off the link

blocks.text: Twice this week the acquirer link dropped in the middle of the day. Each time, a handful of cardholders at other merchants were told "outcome unknown" for purchases the host had approved, and the reversal process then reversed a purchase the host had never received. Both times the log showed a warning from the channel adaptor and nothing else. And one purchase, keyed in as `31.75`, reached the host as an amount nobody had typed.
The client is `PaymentClient` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PaymentClient.java`. Its constructor already gets the packager the link's channel uses. Finish the two places marked `TODO`:

items: `refusal(...)`: the reason a message must not go to the link, or `null`;
`pay(...)`: what happens to such a message, and the `Outcome` the caller gets for it.

blocks.text: When you're done, a message the link can't carry never reaches it, and the caller's outcome says what the host knows about the message. About ten lines in total.
The tests run a real QMUX against a host on the far side of its queues. There is no channel between them, so nothing on the test's side packs the messages: only your code does.

cases.says: a purchase the link can carry goes to the host and its approval is reported
a purchase the host never answers has an unknown outcome and is left for the reversal process
a field longer than the link's packager allows is refused before anything is queued
an amount the packager would accept but the host would misread is refused too, because the packager checks lengths and not content
a refused message never reached the host, so it is reported as refused and not left for reversal
a message without an amount is checked and sent like any other

origin.section: 9.2 A Field the Packager Refuses Fails on the Adaptor's Thread, and Takes the Link With It

concepts: A field the packager refuses fails on the adaptor's sender thread, drops the link by default and reaches the caller only as null; packing a copy first turns it into a refusal before sending.
A packager checks lengths, not content, so a value of the right length can still be wrong.
